patients.summary: Retired postal worker with hypertension, type 2 diabetes, obesity and untreated hyperlipidemia who joined the practice in 2021. From December 2024 he has three ED visits for decompensated heart failure; an echo shows LVEF 35%, and his home regimen of metformin, lisinopril and hydrochlorothiazide never changes.

documents.title: New Patient Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
64 y/o man transferring care; his last PCP office is closing its adult panel and he wanted somewhere he could reach a doctor by phone. Retired from the postal service, was a letter carrier on a walking route for most of it.

PMH: HTN for roughly 12 years. T2DM for about 8 years, metformin only, never on insulin. Weight has been an issue since his 40s. Told his cholesterol was high a few years back, was never put on anything for it.
PSH: appendectomy at 22. Right knee scope at 54, no problems since.
Meds: metformin 1000 mg BID, lisinopril 20 mg daily, HCTZ 25 mg q AM. Brought the bottles; fills line up.
Allergies: sulfa antibiotics, rash years ago.
FH: father had an MI at 70, also HTN. Mother had T2DM and heart failure, died at 81. Brother with HTN and coronary disease.
SH: smoked about a pack a day for 25 years, stopped in 2016. Drinks maybe 1-2 times a month. Lives on his own, drives.
Vaccines: two Pfizer doses this spring at the pharmacy.

ROS: feels fine. No exertional chest discomfort, no breathlessness, no swelling, no polyuria, no foot numbness, no vision change.

Exam: BP 142/88 on recheck. BMI about 34. Well appearing. Fundi not dilated. Heart RRR, no murmur. Lungs clear throughout. Abd obese, soft, healed RLQ scar. No peripheral edema. Feet: skin intact, monofilament felt at all sites, DP and PT pulses 2+.

A/P
1. HTN: a bit above goal on lisinopril + HCTZ. Wants to work on salt first. Recheck next visit, no change today.
2. T2DM: A1c, CMP, urine albumin/creatinine today.
3. Obesity: talked about walking again, he used to cover miles a day.
4. Hyperlipidemia: lipid panel today.
5. Former smoker, 25 pk-yr, quit 2016: eligible for annual low-dose CT, ordered. One-time aortic ultrasound ordered.
6. HCV and HIV screening once, both drawn today.
7. Prior records requested. Colonoscopy he thinks was 2017.
RTC 6 months, sooner for BP if needed.

documents.title: Your lab results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Mr. Yeager, your labs are back. Your A1c is 7.6, a little above where we'd like it, so let's see what more walking does before we think about another medicine. Kidney function and potassium are fine and there is no protein leaking into the urine. LDL cholesterol is 136. Hepatitis C and HIV screens are negative and never need repeating. Talk soon.

documents.title: Records from prior primary care office
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: Received 14 pages from previous PCP office. Contents: medication list (metformin 1000 mg BID, lisinopril 20 mg daily, HCTZ 25 mg daily), allergy list (sulfa - rash), visit notes 2018-2021 for diabetes and BP, and a screening colonoscopy report from 2017: cecum reached, good prep, no polyps, recall 10 years. Routed to PCP.

documents.title: Records review
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Old records reviewed. Nothing new beyond what he told me. Colonoscopy 2017 clean, next due 2027. Health maintenance updated.

reports.study: Low-dose CT chest for lung cancer screening
reports.text: Indication: lung cancer screening; former smoker, 25 pack-years, quit 2016. Technique: low-dose helical CT of the chest without IV contrast. Comparison: none. Findings: No pulmonary nodules. Airways patent. No consolidation or effusion. Heart normal in size. No mediastinal or hilar adenopathy. Visualized upper abdomen unremarkable.
reports.conclusion: Lung-RADS 1, negative. Continue annual screening in 12 months.

documents.title: LDCT result
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Screening CT negative, Lung-RADS 1. Repeat next summer. Pt notified by portal.

reports.text: Indication: abdominal aortic aneurysm screening, male former smoker. Limited ultrasound of the abdominal aorta. The proximal, mid and distal aorta are visualized and measure up to 2.1 cm in maximal outer diameter. No focal dilation. Common iliac arteries normal in caliber.
reports.conclusion: Normal caliber abdominal aorta. No aneurysm.

documents.title: Aorta ultrasound result
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: No AAA. One-time screen complete, no repeat needed.

documents.title: Refill request
documents.author: MA
documents.body: Pharmacy requesting 90-day supplies of metformin, lisinopril and HCTZ so the patient can switch to mail order. Pended for PCP, approved with 3 refills each.

documents.title: Immunizations
documents.author: RN
documents.body: In for high-dose flu (L arm) and Pfizer booster (R arm). Screening questions negative. Sulfa allergy noted, not relevant to these. Observed 15 minutes, no reaction. VIS given.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Follow-up Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
S: Six-month check. Walking most mornings when it isn't icy. Taking all three meds, no missed doses he can think of. No lightheadedness. No thirst or night urination.
O: BP and weight as charted. Heart regular, no murmur. Chest clear. No ankle swelling.
A/P: T2DM, A1c redrawn today. HTN, close to goal; continue lisinopril 20 and HCTZ 25. Pneumococcal: PCV20 given today, that covers him. Next visit around his birthday for the Welcome to Medicare exam.

documents.title: Optometry report
documents.author: optometry
documents.body: Dilated eye examination performed 2022-03-10 for a patient with type 2 diabetes. Allergies on file: sulfa drugs. Acuity 20/25 OD, 20/25 OS with correction. Anterior segments quiet. Lens with early age-related changes. Fundus: optic nerves healthy, maculae flat, no hemorrhages, exudates or neovascularization either eye. Impression: no diabetic retinopathy. Return in one year.

procedures.procedure: Initial preventive physical examination (Welcome to Medicare)

documents.title: Initial Preventive Physical Exam
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
IPPE, within his first year of Medicare Part B (turned 65 last July).
Functional: independent, drives, does his own shopping. No falls. Hearing fine in conversation. Vision: eye exam in March, no retinopathy.
PHQ-2 0. Cognition: no concerns from him, recall 3/3.
Advance directive: none yet; handed him the health care proxy form, he will think about who to name.

Exam: BP and weight as charted, BMI about 34. Ears clear. Heart RRR without murmur. Lungs clear. Abdomen soft. Extremities without edema. Foot exam: monofilament intact bilaterally, pulses palpable, no calluses.

Plan
- Labs: CMP, lipids, A1c, urine albumin/creatinine
- Shingrix #1 today, #2 in the fall
- LDCT due July
- Colonoscopy 2017 normal, due 2027
- Continue metformin, lisinopril, HCTZ

documents.title: Lab results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Francis, labs look about the same as last year. A1c 7.5, kidneys normal, urine protein normal. Keep doing what you're doing. Second shingles shot in the fall with your flu shot.

documents.title: RE: Lab results
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Thanks Doc. The shingles shot knocked me out for a day but I'm fine now. Will do the second one in October.

orders.order: Low-dose CT chest for lung cancer screening

reports.study: Low-dose CT chest for lung cancer screening
reports.text: Indication: annual lung cancer screening. Low-dose noncontrast CT chest. Comparison: 2021-07-20. Findings: Lungs without nodules. No airspace disease. No pleural effusion. Heart size normal. No lymphadenopathy.
reports.conclusion: Lung-RADS 1. Negative. Next annual screen in 12 months.

documents.title: LDCT result
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Negative, Lung-RADS 1 again. Portal note sent.

documents.title: Immunizations
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Three today: high-dose flu L deltoid, bivalent Pfizer booster R deltoid, Shingrix #2 L deltoid lower site. Warned him the Shingrix can make him achy like last time. Waited 15 min, fine. Shingrix series complete.

documents.title: Appointment cancelled
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: Pt called, car is in the shop and he has no ride tomorrow. Moved to the week of 12/12.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Follow-up Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
S: Says the fall got away from him, less walking once the clocks changed, more snacking. Weight up a couple of pounds. Meds unchanged and taken.
O: Vitals as charted. Lungs clear, heart RRR. No edema. Feet look good.
A/P:
T2DM - A1c pending today; if it creeps up we'll talk about a second agent at the next visit. He'd rather try harder on food first.
HTN - acceptable, continue.
RTC 5 months.

documents.title: A1c
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: A1c came back 7.9, up from 7.5. Not alarming but heading the wrong way. Let's recheck in the spring after the holidays are behind you. Kidney labs fine.

documents.title: RE: A1c
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Figured. No more holiday cookies til next year, I promise. See you in May.
